content:
UC boys win three events, finish a very strong second at the State Non-Public A Relays

Results | Race Videos | Photos

The Vikings won the 4×400, shuttle hurdles and the pole vault

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic boys put together several impressive performances and won three events when the Vikings placed a very strong second at Thursday’s Non-Public A Relay Championships at the Bennett Center in Toms River.

UC, which scored in eight of the nine events, won the shuttle hurdles in 31.13, captured the 4×400 in dramatic fashion in 3:27.04, and finished first in the team pole vault as the Vikings piled up 56 points. Christian Brothers Academy finished first with 76.

There were lots of Vikings who sparkled on the track and in the field.

Junior Conor Reilly matched his personal best and school record in the vault when he cleared a meet best 15-0, and had splits of 52.7 in the 4×400 and 24.1 leading off the third-place 4×200

Junior Elijah Brown anchored the third-place 4×800 with a 1:58.7 carry, and went 50.2 in the 4×400.

Freshman Myles Plummer went 51.8 when he came from behind on the anchor leg to catch CBA right at the line to win the 4×400, and split 1:59.6 in the 4×800.

Obadare Animashaun led off the winning shuttle hurdles for UC with a 7.8 split, cleared 12-0 in the vault, and ran a 200 on the fifth-place SMR.

Elijah Abraham anchored the shuttles and 4×200, and ran the 400 leg on the SMR.

Brandon Leslie ran 7.8 in the shuttles, and 23.9 in the SMR. Connor Cooper blasted a 22.9 in the 4×200 and ran on the 4×400. Chinedu Okoro ran 23.6 in the 4×200 and made 5-6 for the fourth-place high jump team. Ryan McLaughlin ripped a 7.3 in the shuttles, and Uchenna Duru (50-7 ¼) and Jared Ware (44-7 ¼) teamed up to place second in the shot put. Duru’s 50-7 ¼ is No. 16 in the state this season.

content:
RACE VIDEOS | RESULTS

The Vikings ran 3:34.35 at Saturday’s meet at Lawrenceville

By Jim Lambert

Union Catholic’s sprint medley relay team went to the Lavino Relays in Lawrenceville on Saturday with one goal in mind. To drop a red hot time.

That’s exactly what they did as the Vikings burned a 3:34.35, the third fastest time in the nation this season by a high school boys team, to finish first. UC finished just ahead of runner-up Lawrenceville, second in a US #4 3:34.71.

The only two teams in the country to run faster than UC are St. Benedict’s Prep of Newark (3:33.46) and Bronxville of N.Y. (3:33.79).

The four runners that cranked out the sizzling time for UC were senior Chinedu Okoro (23.1 for 200), junior Conor Reilly (24.1 for 200), junior Elijah Brown (49.5 for 400), and freshman Myles Plummer (1:57.4 for 800).

In addition to its SMR victory, the Vikings also ran a very fast shuttle hurdle relay, placing second in 31.22, the fourth fastest time by a N.J. team this winter. UC finished just behind the N.J. #3 time of 31.07 run by Nottingham. UC’s four hurdles were Obadare Animashaun, Ryan McLaughlin, Brandon Leslie, and Oluwafemi Asenuga.

The Girls Squad won the 4×200 and 4×400 Relays and finished 2nd in the 4×800 and Long Jump Relays.
-Felicia Quainoo, Avery, Jordan and Sydney McDonald were all on the 4×2 and 4×4 Relay Wins!
-Morgan Jackson, Morgan Williams, Abby Granrath and Jenna Keith were on the 2nd place 4×8 Squad
-Sophomores A’Liyah Thomas and Danielle Rappa combined to place 2nd in Long Jump

content:
The UC Boys & Girls won the Union County Relay Championship on Saturday! The Girls Won their 6th Straight Relay Championship and the Boys Won their 7th in 9 Years

Results | Some Videos

The UC boys capture the Union County Relay title for seventh time in nine years

1/6/2019 12:44:00 PM

The Vikings edged Elizabeth, 55-52

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic boys track and field team, which scored in all eight events, capped off a spectacular all-round performance by placing second in the meet-concluding 4×400-meter relay to clinch the team title at the Union County Relays on Saturday at the Jersey City Armory.

The Vikings edged Elizabeth, 55-52, to capture its first title since 2016 and its seventh title in the past nine years.

Full results are here

Several athletes came up huge for Union Catholic.

Two of the big catalysts for UC were Elijah Brown and Myles Plummer each ran on the first-place distance medley and sprint medley relay teams, and rna a leg on the runner-up 4×400.

Brown, a junior, split 1:55.6 on the 800 leg on the DMR, which crossed first in 10:51.60, ran 50.7 on the SMR, which won in 3:39.54, and had a 50.1 carry in the 400.

Plummer, one of the state’s top freshman, anchored the DMR with a 4:37.5 carry, split 2:00.9 as the anchor on the SMR, and had a 51.5 anchor carry in the 4×400.

Chinedu Okoro, Conor Reilly, and Connor Cooper also had big days for UC.

Okoro ran 23.1 on the SMR, split 24.1 on the fourth-place 4×200, and cleared 5-6 on the runner-up high jump team.

Reilly, one of the state’s top pole vaulters, ran 52.7 in the 4×400 and 23.3 on the fourth-place 4×400.

Cooper had splits of 53.5 for 400 on the DMR, and 24.2 in the 4×200.

In other UC highlights, Matt Axt came up with a clutch 54.1 leg in the 400. Ryan McLaughlin and Brandon Leslie each split 7.5 on the runner-up shuttle hurdle team, Obadare Animashaun led off the shuttle hurdles and ran a 24-6 in the SMR, Oluwafemi Asenuga cleared 5-10 in the high jump, and Uchenna Duru (46-1 1/2), Jared Ware (43-4 1/4) and Ray Lestarchick (39-7) combined to give UC a runner-up finish in the shot put.

UC girls win 5 events, break meet record on way to 6th straight Union County Relay title

 1/6/2019 7:15:00 PM

The Vikings scored 66 out of a possible 80 points

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls track and field team won five races, broke a meet record, and ran a NJ #1 time on the way to winning its sixth straight title at the Union County Relays on Saturday at the Jersey City Armory.

Union Catholic, which scored 66 out of a possible 80 points and outscored runner-up Summit by 34 points, won the distance medley relay in a NJ#1 12:38.83, the 4×200 in a meet record 1:44.86, the 4×400 in 4:06.40, the 4×800 in 9:59.04, and the shuttle hurdles in 33.79. UC also ran a NJ#3 4:14.78 to place second in the sprint medley to Gov. Livingston’s NJ#2 4:13.63.

Several athletes shined for the Vikings.

Jerika Lufrano anchored the DMR with a 5:06.7 carry. Morgan Williams had splits of 2:23.6 in the 4×800 and 2:29.1 in the DMR. Ashleigh Patterson anchored the 4×800 (2:26.8) and 4×400 (62.2).  Khamil Evans ran 59.3 in the SMR and 26.0 in the 4×200. Sydney Tucker split 25.5 in the 4×200 and 25.7 in the SMR. Chi Chi Nkulume went 59.0 in the 4×400 and 26.2 in the 4×200. A’Liyah Thomas cleared 5-0 on the runner-up high jump team, split 8.2 in the shuttles, and went 26.6 in the SMR. Zamira Ysaac anchored the SMR in 2:22.7 and ran 7.9 on the shuttles, and Angelique Williams cleared 5-4 in the HJ.

RESULTS   PHOTOS

Plummer ran a school freshman record and NJ #1 time in the 800

By Jim Lambert

Elijah Brown, Myles Plummer, Conor Reilly and the 4×400-meter relay team all threw down strong performances for the Union Catholic boys track and field team at Saturday’s Marine Corp Holiday Classic at the 168th Street Armory in New York.

Brown, a junior, ran 49.60 to place fifth in the 400, the second fastest time by a NJ athlete this season, and split 49.77 on the fourth-place 4×400 that ran a NJ#2 3:25.00 to qualify for the New Balance National Championships.

Plummer broke his own school freshman record in the 800 by placing sixth in a NJ#1 1:58.74, and anchored the 4×400 in 51.17. Plummer’s 1:58.74 broke his school record of 1:59.71 that he ran at the Essex County Coaches Invit. on Dec. 14 at Ocean Breeze,

Reilly, senior, cleared 14-6 to finish third in the pole vault, and led off the 4×400 with a 52.30 carry in the 4×400. Reilly is currently ranked second in the N.J. in the pole vault with the 15-0 he made earlier this month.

Senior Elijah Abraham also had a strong meet for the Vikings by running 8.19 in the trials of the 55 hurdles and running a 51.74 led in the 4×400.

PHOTOS
RESULTS

UC’s 4×400 relay ran a US#2 3:53.95, and Handlin broke the school record in the pole vault

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls track and field team made its presence felt in a huge way with several eye-popping results at Saturday’s Marine Corp Holiday Classic at the 168th Street Armory in New York.

In the most dramatic finish of the meet, the 4×400-meter relay squad blasted a NJ#1 and US#2 time of 3:53.95 as the Vikings were edged by Bullis of Maryland, who ran a US #1 3:53.90.  Chi Chi Nkulume led off for UC in 59.64, Leena Morant followed with a 57.31, Sydney Tucker then ran 59.49, and Khamil Evans anchored in 57.49.

UC also ripped a hot time in the 4×800 as combined to run a NJ#3 9:54.70 to place third. Jerika Lufrano led off with a 2:20.89 carry, Abby Granath ran 2:27.92, Megan McCabe went 2:37.54, and Zoe Lee anchored in 2:28.34.

Lufrano’s lead off leg in the 4×800 was part of big day for the senior. She also won the mile with a NJ#1 time of 5:04.09.

Senior Hope Handlin continued climbing to new heights in the pole vault as the senior smashed her own school record by placing sixth with a clearance of 11-0, which ties for her No. 2 in N.J. this season. Handlin broke her own school mark of 10-6 that she set earlier this month.

Rising star A’Liyah Thomas had a great day for the Vikings. The sophomore placed ninth in the long jump with 17-0, matched her personal best by clearing 5-0 to place 10th in the high jump, and ran a huge personal best of 8.68 in the trials of the 55 hurdles.

In other highlights for UC, Morant placed sixth in the girls 800 in a NJ#2 2:19.17, Evans, the state leader in the 300 at 40,23, was ninth in the 300 in 40.83, Tucker placed eighth in the  200 in 26.17, and Felicia Quainoo was eight in the 55 hurdles in 8.48.

Saturday’s meet put the finishing on a busy and great weekend for the Vikings at the Armory.

At Friday’s New Jersey Catholic Track Conference Relays, Zamira Ysaac, Quainoo, Avery Jordan and Thomas combined to run a NJ#2 31.64 in the shuttle hurdles to place second to Paramus Catholic’s 30.84.

By Jim Lambert

Megan McCabe placed seventh in the 3,000-meter run and Matt Granizo dropped a big personal best in the boys 3,200 to highlight action for the Union Catholic track and field teams at the North Shore Invitational on Wednesday at the 168th Street Armory in New York.

content:
Reilly smashes school record, Brown wins to lead UC boys at Jim Mitchell Invitational

Reilly cleared 15-0 in the vault, and Brown and Plummer broke school class records

By Jim Lambert

Conor Reilly broke the school record in the pole vault, and Elijah Brown, who won the 600-meter run, and Myles Plummer each shattered school class records when the Union Catholic boys competed at the Jim Mitchell on Friday night at the Jim Mitchell Invitational at the 168th Street Armory in New York.

Reilly, a junior, cleared a personal best 15-0 to place second on misses in the pole vault to break the school indoor record of 14-6 that he set last year. Reilly, who also placed seventh in te 30 in 36.74, is now ranked No. 2 in New Jersey this season in the pole vault with his 15-0.

Brown broke the UC junior class record when he rallied to edge Charles Dasilva of Pope John to win the 600 in a NJ #1 1:22.13, just missing the school record of 1:22.03 set in 2016 by Trae Robinson. Brown’s 1:22.13 shattered the junior class record of 1:23.38 set in 1016 by Greg Gibbs.

Plummer, who broke the school freshman class record in the 800 with a 1:59.71, earlier this season, added the school freshman record in the 1,000 when he finished seventh in the 1,000 in a NJ #2 2:38.02. The former freshman record of 2:46.97 was set by Justin Cadas in 2015.

In other highlights, Ryan McLaughlin placed third in the 55 hurdles in 7.83, Uchenna Duru was second in the shot put at 44-8 3.4, Jared Ware was fourth with a 44-2 1/4.

Morant, Lufrano and Handlin break school records, Evans and Quainoo and 4×200 win at Jim Mitchell Invit.

Morant won the 600 in a school record 1:34.07 and Handlin broke the PV record, and Lufrano took down the 1,000 record

By Jim Lambert

Leena Morant, who won the 600-meter run, Jerika Lufrano and Hope Handlin all took down school records, and Khamil Evans, Felicia Quainoo and the 4×200-meter relay all scored victories for the Union Catholic girls at the Jim Mitchell Invitational on Friday night at the 168th Street N.Y. Armory.

Morant, a junior, won the 600 in 1:34.07, the second fastest time by a N.J. runner this season, to break the UC school record of 1:34.66 set in 2016 by Amari Onque-Shabazz.

Handlin, a senior, cleared a personal best and NJ #5 10-6 to place second in the pole vault as she shattered the school record of 9-6 that she shared with Mia Bennett-Jones. Jones made 9-6 last year, and Handlin matched the record when she made 9-6 at the Essex County Coaches Season Opener on Dec. 14.

Lufrano, a senior, took over the state lead this season when she finished second in the 1,000 in 2:57.67, which broke the school record of 3:02.17 that Lufrano ran last year.

Evans, Quainoo, and the UC 4×200 relay team also sparkled.

Evans, a senior, won the 300 in a personal best 40.23, the fastest time in N.J. this season, and Quainoo crossed the line first in the 55 hurdles in 8.46, the third fastest time in the state this winter.

UC lit up the track in the 4×200 as Sydney Tucker, A’Liyah Thomas, Quainoo and Evans blasted a 1:43.54, the No. 1 time in N.J. and No. 7 time in the nation so far this season.

In other highlights, Tucker was third in the 300 in 40.73, Zamira Ysaac placed third in the 600 in 1:38.18, Ashleigh Patterson finished fourth in the 600 in 1:38.24, and Avery Jordan was sixth in the hurdles in 8.81 and ninth in the 300, and Morgan Williams was seventh in the 600.

content:
Double winner Tucker helps UC girls roll to season opening victory

The Vikings won the Essex County Coaches Season Opener by more than 100 points

By Jim Lambert

Sydney Tucker won two sprint races with personal best times and Union Catholic picked up victories from five other athletes as the Vikings overpowered the competition on the way to a huge victory in its season opener at the Essex County Track Coaches Invitational at Ocean Breeze on Friday on Staten Island.

Tucker, a junior, won the 55-meter dash in 7.30 and the 200 in 25.90 to help the Vikings roll to a 157-38 victory over runner-up West Orange.

UC, favored to win its fifth straight Non-Public A  State Track and Field title this season, also received victories from Khamil Evans, Leena Morant, Hope Handlin, A’Liyah Thomas, and Felicia Quainoo, and the 4×400 was also victorious (4:05.90).

Evans won the 400 in 58.35, Morant led a 1-2-3-4 finish for the Vikings in the 800 with a winning time of 2:19.92, Handlin won the pole vault at 9-6, Thomas captured the high jump (4-10) and was second in the long jump (16-3 1/2), and Quainoo won the 55 hurdles in 8.49.

In other highlights, freshman Sydney McDonald made a great high school debut by placing third in the 20 in 26.75, and fifth in the 55 dash in 7.60. Angelique Williams finished second in the high jump (4-10), fourth in the long jump (16-1), and was sixth in the 55 hurdles in 9.01. Isabella Gray came up with a third place finish for the Vikings in the pole vault by clearing 9-0.

content:
Reilly, Plummer, and Brown sparkle to lead UC boys T&F team to victory in season opener

The Vikings defeated runner-up St. Peter’s Prep, 79-53

By Jim Lambert

Myles Plummer, who shattered a school record, and Conor Reilly and Elijah Brown were all double winners to spark the Union Catholic boys track and field team to victory in its season opener on Friday at the Essex County Coaches Invitational at the Ocean Breeze Athletic Complex.

The Vikings outscored runner-up St. Peter’s Prep, 79-53, to capture the team title. 

Plummer, one of the top rising stars in New Jersey, won the 800-meter run in a school freshman record 1:59.71, the No. 1 time in the state so far this season, and also ran on the winning 4×400 relay (3:31.82). Plummer’s 1:59.71 not only broke the UC freshman indoor record of 2:03.64 set in 2014 by Greg Gibbs, but it’s also superior to the school outdoor freshman record of 2:00.39 that Gibbs ran.  

Reilly, a junior who one of the state’s premier pole vaulters, led a 1-2-3-5 finish for the Vikings in the vault by clearing 14-0, and he also split 52.5 on the leadoff leg of the 4×400. Brown, a junior who is one of the state’s top sprinters, won the 400 with a New Jersey No. 1 time of 49.88, and anchored the victorious 4×400.   

In other highlights, senior Ryan McLaughlin placed second in the 55 hurdles in 8.07, Obadare Animashaun finished second in the pole vault (12-6) and was fifth in the hurdles in 8.30, Justin Lopez placed third in the pole vault (12-0), Christopher Robateau was fifth in the vault (9-0), Elijah Abraham finished sixth in the hurdles in 8.36 and ran on the winning relay, and Chinedu Okoro placed sixth in the 200 in 23.47.

content:
Lestarchick throws huge personal best for UC boys at Rebel Shot Put Invit.

The senior unloaded a 42-0 to place seventh at Howell High School

By Jim Lambert

Senior Ray Lestarchick unloaded a huge personal best on his final throw to finish seventh to highlight action for Union Catholic at the Rebel Shot Put Series on Friday night at Howell High School

Lestarchick launched a 42-0 on his last attempt to shatter his previous personal best of 36-0 that he hit at the Union County J.V. Championships last spring.

The 42-0 by Lestarchick was not only a big PR, but it also places him No. 3 in the Union County shot put rankings after the opening weekend of the season.

Also in the boys Senior Division competition, Jared Ware placed 8th for UC with a throw of 41-6 1/2, and Uchenna Duru also threw 41-61 1/2 for UC to place ninth.

In the girls Senior Division, Rebecca Penevolpe threw 24-9 for Union Catholic to place 18th.

PLEASE READ EVERYTHING CAREFULLY AND FOLLOW ALL INSTRUCTIONS. THANK YOU

  1.  If you haven’t already, please join the WINTER TRACK & FIELD REMIND GROUP
  2. Fill Out this Form Today (It is Very Important): ATHLETE INFORMATION FORM (WINTER T+F)
  3. If you are interested in Ordering Meals for Next Week, today is the deadline. CLICK HERE FOR INFORMATION ABOUT MEALS
  4. Read Below about Meet Information for Saturday (12/8)

Saturday, December 8th, 2018
Lawrenceville Scrimmage
The Lawrenceville School

Arrive at UC: 11:00am   Start Time: 2:00pm
-If you do not have a uniform it will be distributed at 11:00am before we leave for the meet.
-Girls, please wear black 1/2 tights. We do not have any left. If you don’t have black, wear another color. We are waiting on a shipment of new tights.
-Boys, bring black half tights or shorts…just in case.

Pre-Meet Information for Friday: DISTANCE…Recovery Run (Normal Distance) with 6 Strides. LONG SPRINTS…20 Minute Run + 3×200 at 800 Race Pace with 3 ‘ Rest   SPRINTS…4×100 at 400 Race Pace with 3′ Rest  or  3×200 at Tempo Pace with 3′ Rest.  THROWS: Drills     EVERYONE: STRETCH

Meet Entries Below – Note: 4×400 Relay Lineups will be set during the meet.

Order of Running Events:
 
(Girls followed by Boys)
4×800 (1 team each)
55HH (5 entries per team)
55M (5 entries per team)
1600 (5 entries per team)
400 (5 entries per team)
800 (5 entries per team)
200 (5 entries per team)
4X400 (A & B teams)

* We will use two HJ mats immediately following the 55m (girls will jump on the mat positioned near the timing table). Girls – 4’3”, 4’6 and then by 2’ – 4’8”; Boys 5’3”, 5’6 and then by 2” – 5’8”
* Girls will throw first in the shot (3 throws).
*  Long jump will run as a co-ed open pit starting at 2pm (duration = 1 hour; 3 jumps).
*  TJ co-ed open pit will start at approximately 3:20 (3 jumps).
*  Pole vault (co-ed) will begin immediately after 55m and start at 6’6. PV LIMITED TO 3 ENTRIES PER TEAM

author: Michael McCabe
classList: post-13782 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-all-posts category-winter-track-and-field
excerpt: The Winter Track & Field Season begins on Monday, November 19th. Please make sure all Online Paperwork, Physical and Fees are submitted. 2018-2019 Winter […]
content:
The Winter Track & Field Season begins on Monday, November 19th. Please make sure all Online Paperwork, Physical and Fees are submitted.

2018-2019 Winter Track & Field Schedule

Directions for Submitting Union Catholic Athletic Paperwork

UNION CATHOLIC HAS A NEW WAY TO REGISTER FOR SPORTS!!!

To access the team registration page, please go to https://ucrhs-ar.rschooltoday.com/

Once on that page, read the information provided for any updates/instructions.

Click the “Athletic Team Registration” icon to begin.

Create a family account (this will be saved so that you can add other children to the same family and can re-register students for other sports/seasons without having to re-enter all of your family information).

Through the Activity Registration, register a new student by entering information about your student and select the sport(s) that he/she wishes to play.

In Step 4, download the physical paperwork to be filled out by the doctor and handed in to the school in person along with the participation fee.

Complete information for all 6 Steps and submit. Paperwork will then be completed. Students will be cleared once participation fees and physicals have also been handed in, and will be noted on each student’s account.

content:
UC’s Mike McCabe chosen as N.J. Girls T&F Coach of the Year by the USTFCCCA

7/10/2018 10:08:00 AM

The Vikings finished the season undefeated and ranked No. 1 in N.J.

By Jim Lambert

Mike McCabe, Union Catholic’s head track and field coach, added to his legacy as one of the premier high school coaches in the country when he was recently chosen by the U.S. Track & Field and Cross Country Coaches Association as the New Jersey’s girls track and field coach for this past season.

This is the fifth year that the USTFCCCA has selected a boys and girls Coach of the Year for each state, and McCabe has been honored every year. After being chosen as the N.J. boys Coach of the Year by the USTFCCCA in 2013, McCabe, who completed his 15th year as head coach at UC, has now captured the girls award four straight years.

The award is chosen based on how a team finishes at their state championships, the number of different events in which athletes qualified for the state championships,, individual championships, and how a team stacks up to its performances in previous years.

McCabe led the Vikings to the No. 1 ranking in the state this past spring, its fourth straight Non-Public A state title, and its fourth straight undefeated campaign.

One of the biggest highlights of the season came when UC broke its own state record by running 58.30 to place fourth at the New Balance Nationals at the University of North Carolina A&T in Greensboro, N.C.

UC’s 58.30 broke the state record of 58.38 that it set at the 2015 East Coast Relays in Randolph Amaya Chadwick, led off for UC with a 13.9 split. Felicia Quainoo then went 14.2. A’Liyah Thomas followed with a 15.4, and Brianna Ewing anchored with a 14.6.

Also at New Balance Nationals, UC finished ninth in the distance medley relay in a school record and a NJ #2 12:09.53, ninth in a school record and NJ #4 47.38, sixth in the 800 sprint medley in 1:46.13, and ninth in the 1,600 sprint medley relay in a NJ #2 4:03.66.

In the DMR, junior Alexandra Borik led off in 3:46.91. Freshman Avery Jordan followed with a 1:00.98 400 carry. Sophomore Leena Morant then ran 2:18.94 in the 800, and junior Jerika Lufrano anchored in 5:02.72. The 12:09.53 shattered the school record of 12:17.53 that the Vikings ran at April’s Blue Devil Relays in Westfield

In the 4×100, Kira Alexander, Sydney Tucker, Khamil Evans, and Felicia Quianoo combined to run 47.38, breaking the school record of 47.42 that the Vikings ran at the Penn Relays in April.

UC also ran NJ #2 times in both the 4×400 (3:47.08) and the 4×800 (a school record 9:10.04).

Individually, Chadwick won the high hurdles at the Meet of Champions in a NJ #1 and personal best 13.77. Lufrano broke three school records with times of 5:02.38 in the 1,600, 10:49.87 in the 3,200, and 17:45.79 in the 5,000. She also won the 3,200 at the state Non-Public A Championships, and was seventh in the 3,200 at the M of C. Morant ran a NJ #2 2:10.61 to place second in the 800 at the M of C..

UC’s Amaya Chadwick wins high hurdles at Meet of Champions

6/11/2018 8:33:00 AM

Morant, Evans, Lufrano, Ysaac also star for the Vikings

Jim Lambert

Amaya Chadwick experienced a wide range of emotions after she crossed the finish line in the 100-meter high hurdles at Saturday’s NJSIAA Meet of Champions at North Burlington High School in Columbus.

At first, the senior at Union Catholic thought she lost her dramatic battle with Reanda Richards of West Essex in a race that was impossible to tell who won as they both leaned across the line at the same time.

But then about 10 minutes after the race concluded, Chadwick found out she won the race in one of the closest races in meet history. Chadwick and Richards were both timed in 13.77.

The victory was especially sweet for Chadwick after she had come so agonizingly close to winning at the M of C in the past. Chadwick was second at the 2016 and 2017 outdoor M of C in the high hurdles, and was second at the 2017 Indoor M of C in the 55 hurdles.

“I was so upset right after the race because I thought I was going to be second again,” said the Purdue-bound Chadwick. “Then when I found out I won I was relieved and excited. This was my last chance to win this and to do with my fastest time in a race that close is just so crazy. My emotions have been all over the place. I am just thankful to finally win this on my last try.

Watch a video interview with Chadwick here

Chadwick wasn’t the only Viking to star in the meet.

Sophomore Leena Morant finished second in the 800 in a personal best and NJ #3 2:10.61, just off the school record of 2:10.03 set in 2015 by Amari Onque-Shabazz, and she split 55.8 on the runner-up 4×400 that ran 3:47.08.

Junior Jerika Lufrano broke her own school record in the 3,200 by running 10:49.87 to place seventh. Zamira  Ysaac ran 1:02.41 to finish seventh in the 400 hurdles and split 57.4 on the 4×400. Khamil Evans finished third in the 400 in 55.47 and anchored the 4×400 in 55.3. Avery Jordan led off the 4×400 for UC with a 58.1 carry.

content:
The 14-9 1/4 by Reilly on Friday broke a 37 year-old record

By Jim Lambert

A few days ago, Conor Reilly was doing a little research on what the state sophomore record in the pole vault was.

When he discovered that it was 14-9, the sophomore at Union Catholic flashed a huge grin.

After making 15-0 in practice this season, Reilly knew it was just a matter of time before that record would be his.

The time came on Friday when Reilly scaled over the bar at 14-9 1/4 at the Union County Conference Championships at Gov. Livingston High School to become the No. 1 sophomore vaulter in N.J. outdoor history.

WATCH REILLY’S RECORD BREAKING VAULT 

Reilly’s 14-9 1/4 clearance broke the state sophomore record that was set 37 years ago when Ray Maragni of Seton Hall Prep  made 14-9 in 1981. The 14-9 1/4 also vaulted Reilly to NJ #1 this season (not including dual meet marks) and is US #19 among all sophomores.

The 5-8 Reilly, who came into the indoor season with a PR of 13-0 and climbed up to 14-6 during this past winter, now has his sights set on making 15-0 and beyond this season.

Reilly, who is the starting goalie on the UC soccer team, has always had a flare for doing things in the air. And like many great vaulters, he has a strong gymnastics background.
“I think the thing that makes me so successful in vaulting is that I’ve had a long career in gymnastics,” said Reilly. “I did gymnastics for like nine years, and it (the pole vault) just feels very natural for me.”

Reilly’s gymnastics experience was responsible for helping to get him introduced to vaulting.

When he attended a track camp at Union Catholic in eighth grade, Andrew Ghizzone was working the camp. Ghizzone won the pole vault for Union Catholic by clearing 16-0 at the 2014 outdoor Meet of Champions, and he’s now starring at the University of Colorado,

“Andrew recognized me from gymnastics and said I should try the vault,” said Reilly. “I’ve loved it ever since.”

Njoroge will play soccer at Jefferson University, Samuels will continue her T&F career at Wagner

By Jim Lambert

Two members of Union Catholic’s Class of 2018 gathered with their families, coaches, classmates, and school administrators for a special ceremony in the main lobby of the school on Friday morning to sign their National Letters of Intent.

Josh Njoroge signed to play soccer at Jefferson University in Philadelphia, and Christina Samuels signed to continue her track and field career at Wagner College on Staten Island.

Njoroge, who lives in Union, combined great field vision, remarkable balls skills, and tremendous leadership to become one of the top defensive soccer players in Union County this past season.

The rock steady play in the back by Njoroge, who was a captain for coach Tim Breza‘s squad , was a big reason why Union Catholic won its second straight Sky Division title in the Union County Conference, and finished with a 10-4-3 record.

“This really means the world to me,” said Njoroge, who wants to be an occupational therapist. “To see all my hard work, the blood, sweat and tears pay off like this feels great.

Samuels, one of the top throwers in Union County, through a personal best of 35-9 ½ in the shot put when she was fourth at the Union County Indoor Championships this past winter, and has a personal best of 102-10 in the discus, which came when Samuels was fifth at the Union County Championships last spring.

Samuels, who has helped the Vikings win several county and state titles during her great career at UC, placed third in the discus at the Union County Conference Championships yesterday.

“I’m really proud of myself because I never really thought I’d be going to a Division 1 school for track,” said Samuels, who lives in Roselle. “But I really worked hard this past year to make this happen, so this really means a lot to me.”

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic boys track and field team received several great performances on its way to a second straight title and seventh championship in the past eight years at Friday’s 75th Union County Relays on Friday’s at Gary Kehler Stadium in Westfield.

The Vikings piled up 107 points to outscore runner-up Rahway by 30 points.

There were lots of highlights for UC.

The trio of Uchenna Duru, who threw a huge PR and NJ #15 of 156-0, Brandon Patterson (138-2), and David Saggio (129-0) combined to win the discus  with a school record total 423-2. The old school record of 419-6 set in 2014.

Animashaun also blasted a 22.5 on the 4×200 that finished first in a NJ #6 1:29.42, and ran on the runner-up shuttle hurdles.

The 4×100 team ran a NJ #5 42.80 to place second.

Trevor Garrity ran a 2:02 on the anchor of the third-place sprint medley, 2:03 on the third-place 4×800, and 4:44 on the third-place 4×1600.

Krishna White cleared a meet best 6-4 to lead the Vikings to a runner-up finish in the high jump, and went 45-9 to hellp UC get second in the triple jump.

Justin Cadas went 3:14 on the runner-up distance medley relay, and 1:57 in the 4×800.
 

UC girls dominate Union County Relays, roll to fourth straight title

 5/6/2018 9:25:00 AM

The Vikings won seven events on the track and smashed two meet records

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls track and field team broke two meets records and won eight events during a dominating performance at the 75th Union County Relays when the Vikings rolled to its fourth straight title on Friday at Gary Kehler Stadium in Westfield.

The Vikings, which received contributions from several athletes, won with 99 1/2 points. Westfield was second with 56.

On the opening day of competition on Thursday, UC broke meet records in both the distance medley relay and the 4×100 relay.

In the DMR, Alexandra Borik ran 3:47.9 (a 14 second personal best), Ashleigh Paterson ran a PR of 59.1, Morgan Jackson went 2:20.2 and Jerika Lufrano anchored in 5:08.0 for a meet record 12:17.53, tied for No. 2 in N.J. this season. The former meet record of 12:27.81 was set by New Providence in 2016 .

UC, using Sydney Tucker, Kira Alexander, Khamil Evans, and Amaya Chadwick, also 47.51 to break its own meet record of 47.76 set last year.

The UC girls now own 8 of the meet records nine meet records on the track. The only one the Vikings don’t own is the 3×400 hurdles.

The Vikings also ran NJ #1 times to win the 4×200 in 1:40.23 and the sprint medley in 4:07.45, and captured the 4×400 in 3:54.52, the 4×800 in 9:46.01 the 3×400 records in 3:20.44, the triple jump with a combined 101-2 1/4.

In the SMR, junior Khamil Evans blasted a 56.1 400 leg, and Leena Morant split 2:19.0, and soph. Zamira Ysaac ran a meet best 1:04.37 in the 400 hurdles, and Tucker ripped a 24.1 in the 4×200. Tyler Scott of UC leaped a meet best 35-7 3/4 in the triple jump.

And for anyone that thinks the Vikings won’t be as strong next year, the winning 4×800 and DMR teams and the runner-up 4×1,600 team didn’t use any seniors.

The UC girls now own NJ #1 times in four events-the 4×100 (47.42), 4×200 (1:40.23), 4×800 (9:10.04), and sprint medley (4:07.45), and are NJ #2 in the DMR (12:17.53) and 4×400  (3:54.38).

The Vikings ran the 59th fastest 4×400 team out of 536 teams

By Jim Lambert

PHILADELPHIA – Union Catholic’s Brandon Patterson placed seventh in the shot put and the Vikings 4×400-meter relay team ran one of the fastest times of the meet at the 124th Penn Relays at Franklin Field.

Patterson, a senior, placed seventh in the shot put with his throw of 57-11 1/2, and the 4×400 relay team, despite a dropped baton, still ran 3:23.05, the 12th fastest time among all N.J. teams and the 59th fastest time among the 536 teams that competed.

The UC 4×400 team consisted of Daryl Miller, who ran 50.34, Elijah Brown, who dropped a blistering 47.84, Makay Johnson, who split 50.10, and Christian Albanese, who anchored in 54.78.

author: Michael McCabe

content:
By Jim Lambert

PHILADELPHIA – The Union Catholic girls put the finishing touches on its fantastic three days at the Penn Relays by placing a very impressive second in the Tri-State 4×100 final on Saturday at Franklin Field.

The foursome of Kira Alexander, Sydney Tucker, Khamil Evans and Amaya Chadwick combined to run 47.55 to place just behind the 47.39 run by the winner, Cheltenham of Wyncote, Pa. It was the second final in two days for UC’s 4×100. On Friday, the Vikings, running without Evans and Chadwick, placed ninth in the Northeast 4×100 final on Friday in 49.49

The 47.55 run in the Tri-State race by UC is just off the NJ #1 time and school record time of 47.42 they ran to win its 4×100 qualifying heat on Thursday. It was the second 4×100 Tri-State race in three years at Penn for UC. In 2016, the Vikings placed fourth in 48.18.

While the appearances in the two 4×100 finals were huge accomplishments for UC, the biggest highlight of the meet for the Vikings came when it made history by running
in its first ever 4×800 Championship of America race on Friday. UC earned the fifth and final medal in the 4×800 C of A with a time 9:10.40.

UC qualified for the 4×800 C of A by running a NJ #1 and Union County record 9:10.04 to place second in its qualifying heat on Thursday. UC used ???Ashleigh Patterson, Leena Morant, Jerika Lufrano, Zamira Ysaac and Morgan Jackson over the two days in the 4×800.

There’s more.

In addition to the 4×100, and 4×800, UC also ran a NJ #1 3:54.38 in the 4×400 on Thursday. So the Vikings left Franklin Field as the fastest relay team in N.J. in all three races-the 4×100, 4×400, 4×800, a remarkable feat.

Evans, a junior, was very happy with how her team performed in the 4×100.

Chadwick said she thinks UC exceeded expectations.

“I think there are people that might be surprised by what we did here in the 4×100, 4×400 and 4×800,” said the Purdue-bound Chadwick. “But we knew what we were capable of and know how much more we can do. This is just the start of things for our team.”

Evans, who ran on the 4×400 along with Tucker, Felicia Quianoo and Mia Bennett-Jones, is very proud of how her team ran in the 4×100.

“I never ran a 4×100 in my life until last week (at the Blue Devil Classic in Westfield) and Amaya just started racing last week after missing most of indoors, so we know we can go faster after we work with each other more,” said Evans. “So to get second today is a good result, but it’s also made us want to work even harder.”

Chadwick feels that it’s just a matter of time before UC breaks the Union County 4×100 record of 47.07 set by Summit when the Hilltoppers finished first at the Meet of Champions last June.

“I know we can go under 47,” said the Purdue-bound Chadwick. “We might even go under 47 at the county relays next week.”

UC earns final medal with dramatic 5th place finish in 4×800 C of A race at Penn Relays

4/27/2018 3:48:00 PM

The Vikings edged Ridge to win the battle for N.J. supremacy

Jim Lambert

PHILADELPHIA – Union Catholic’s Zamira Ysaac was a step behind Kaitlyn Van Baalen of Ridge with 75 meters left in Friday’s 4×800 Championship of America race at the 124th Penn Relays at Franklin Field.

But she didn’t stay there for very long.

Ysaac, fueled by UC’s loss to Ridge at last month’s New Balance Indoor Nationals, dug down deep and made a huge push to pull even and eventually pass Van Baalen to bring the Vikings across fifth in 9:10.40. Ridge, which won the New Balance Indoor National title in 9:08.07 with UC second in 9:13.90, placed sixth in 9:10.65. Holmwood Tech of Jamaica won its second straight title and meet record 11th title by almost nine seconds in 8:48.33.

Not only did UC avenge its loss to Ridge in the battle for New Jersey supremacy, but by placing fifth, UC nabbed the final medal that was awarded in the 12-team 4×800.

“They (Ridge) beat us indoors, so we really wanted to finish ahead of them this time and be the top New Jersey team, so I just pushed as hard as I could to get ahead of her,” said Ysaac, a sophomore who split 2:18.79.

This was the first time ever that UC ran in the girls 4×800 C of A, which it qualified for by running a Union County record 9:10.04 in Thursday’s qualifying heats, and the third straight year that a UC girls team ran in a C of A race. UC placed third in the 4xx40 C of A in 2016 and last year.

With five underclassmen in its lineup over the past two days, the Vikings left Franklin Field feeling very proud of what they did and confident that it has the potential to contend for its first C of A title in school history over the next couple years.

“We are all young and this was a great experience for us to build off of,” said sophomore Leena Morant, who ran a 2:13.16 second leg. “We have a lot of girls with lots of talent, and we all know if that we all keep working hard we can be right back here next year battling with the top teams.”

UC’s first leg was sophomore Ashleigh Patterson, who split 2:20.21, and junior Jerika Lufrano ran a a personal best 2:18.26 third leg. Sophomore Morgan Jackson anchored on Thursday with a 2:20.8 carry.

“I’m really proud of how we all ran,” said Patterson. “We gave it all we had, and to finish fifth against all these great teams and get a medal is a great accomplishment.”

UC girls qualified for 3 finals and ran fastest NJ times in 3 races at Penn Relays

The Vikings advanced to the 4×800 C of A, two 4×100 finals and ran the top NJ times in 4×100, 4×400 and 4×800

By Jim Lambert

PHILADELPHIA – The Union Catholic girls have a history of making their presence felt on the biggest track and field stages.

The opening day of the 124th Penn Relays on Thursday at historic Franklin Field proved to be no different as UC once again showed the crowd of 22,862 that even without Olympian Sydney McLaughlin (now starring at the University of Kentucky) the Vikings are one of the best programs in the country.

Showcasing its great range and depth, the Vikings used 10 different athletes to qualify for the 4×800 Championship of America race for the first time ever, two 4×100 finals, and they broke one county record and ran the fastest times among all New Jersey squads in the 4×100, 4×400, and 4×800.

UC’s remarkable triple started in the morning when the all underclassmen quartet of Jerika Lufrano, Leena Morant, Zamira Ysaac, and Morgan Jackson ran a Union County record 9:10.04 to place second in its heat and qualify for Friday’s Championships of America race. This is the third straight year that UC will compete in a girls C of A race. The Vikings, with McLaughlin on the anchor, placed third in the 4×400 C of A in 2016 and ’17.

A few hours later, Kira Alexander, Sydney Tucker, Khamil Evans, and Amaya Chadwick teamed up to win its heat in a school record 47.42 to qualify for Friday’s Northeast Championship and Saturday’s Tri-State Championship.

The Vikings capped off its memorable trifecta when the foursome of Evans (57.35), Tucker (58.11), Felicia Quianoo (59.15) and Mia Bennett-Jones (59.78) placed fifth in its heat in 3:54.38, the 16th fastest time among the 611 teams that competed and the ninth fastest among U.S. teams.

UC’s 9:10.04, 47.22, and 3:54.38 are all the fastest times run by a NJ this season.

“It was a real team effort,” said UC coach Mike McCabe. “The girls are reaping the rewards of their hard work and dedication to the team.”

UC girls smash Union County record, advance to 4×800 C of A at Penn Relays

Jerika Lufrano, Leena Morant, Zamira Ysaac, and Morgan Jackson combined to run 9:10.04

By Jim Lambert

PHILADELPHIA – The Union Catholic girls stormed its way into the 4×800 Championship of America race in record breaking fashion at Thursday’s 124th Penn Relays at historic Franklin Field.

The Vikings foursome of Jerika Lufrano, Leena Morant, Zamira Ysaac, Morgan Jackson not only took down the school record, but its time of 9:10.04 also shattered the Union County record as UC placed second in its qualifying heat with the fourth fastest time among the 12 qualifiers for Friday’s final at 1:05 p.m.

UC’s 9:10.04, No. 5 in the nation this season, broke the Union County record of 9:12.9 that was set by Summit in 1981. The former UC school record of 9:13.42 was set during the 2015 indoor season.

This marks the third straight year that a UC girls team has advanced to a Championship of America race and the first time the girls 4×800 team has advanced here. The UC girls 4×400 team, led by Olympian Sydney McLaughlin, placed third the past two years in the C of A. It’s also the fifth time in the past five years that UC will have a team in a C of A race. In 2014, the UC boys ran in both the 4×400 and 4×800 C of A, a remarkable feat.

So how did the UC girls all underclassmen 4×800 relay team make the prestigious C of A?

Running in the first qualifying heat of the day, Lufrano, a junior, led off with a 2:20.38 split. Morant, a sophomore, then cranked out a personal best 2:11.55, the second fastest split of the day, to move the team into second place. Sophomore Ysaac followed with a personal best 2:17.33 to put UC in front. Jackson, a sophomore, closed it out for UC with a PR of 2:20.80 as she came across the line a half step behind Dasia Wilson of Neumann Goretti High School of Philadelphia, which ran 9:09.54.

The only other teams among the 64 that competed in the 4×800 that ran faster than UC were defending champion Holmwood Tech of Jamaica (9:08.49) and Padua Academy (9:08.72).

“Our goal was all four of us to put it together and make the final,” said Morant. “We feel like if we all ran collectively strong we could go under 9:20, so to go 9:10 is a big deal for us. I am very proud of how all of us ran and we will be striving to run faster tomorrow and she what we can do.”

Morant said she and her teammates were out to prove that UC isn’t just a sprint school.

“We always been known as a sprint team, so to come out here and make it to the finals in a different race and be the first girls team from Union Catholic to make it to the final in a 4×800 makes this even more special,” said Morant.

UC girls break 3 school records, win 3 events at Blue Devil Classic

The girls won the shuttle hurdles, 4×100 and DMR

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls tuned up for this week’s Penn Relays by winning three events and breaking three school records at the 30th Blue Devil Classic on Saturday at Gary Kehler Stadium in Westfield.

The Vikings captured the shuttle hurdles in a NJ #2 1:02.74, the 4×100 in a NJ# 3 48.69, and the distance medley relay in a NJ # 3 and school record 12:27.90. The old DMR school record of 12:33.09 was set last year. In addition to the DMR school record, the Vikings also broke school records in the three-person team discus and three-person team pole vault.

In the shuttle hurdles, senior Amaya Chadwick, who returned to the track earlier in the week after a hamstring injury sidelined her for most of the indoor season, led off in 14.0 to put the Vikings ahead to stay. Freshman A’Liyah Thomas had a strong 15.5 leg on the shuttles. Junior Khamil Evans had a strong meet for UC. She ran the third leg on the 4×100 and cranked out a 57.8 in the DMR. Also in the DMR, UC had splits of 3:50.1 from Leena Morant, 2:21.8 from Zamira Ysaac, and 5:17.2 from Jerika Lufrano.

In the discus, Christine Samuels (102-6), Bella Giacobbe (79-2), and Danielle Torres (63.3) combined for a school record 244-11, breaking the mark of 237-10 set in 2010. In the pole vault, Danielle Rappa cleared a school freshman record 7-6, and Hope Handlin and Isabella Gray also made 7-6 for a school record total of 22-6. Tyler Scott leaped a school senior class record 35-5 3/4 in the triple jump.

White and Patterson win to help propel UC boys T&F team to title at Bullis Invit.

Brown, Abraham, Saggio, and Duro also excel for the Vikings

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic boys track and field made a big statement by winning the team title at the prestigious Bullis Bulldog Invitational on Saturday in Potomac, Maryland.

Brandon Patterson won the shot put with a throw of 55-0 1/4, and was fifth in the discus (136-9) as the Vikings outscored Dover of Maryland, 64-43. Krishna White also had a big day in the jumps for UC. He won the triple jump with a PR and NJ #2 3 46-7 3/4, was fourth in the high jump (6-2), and went 21-0 in the high jump.

Also for UC, sophomore Elijah Brown was third in the 400 with a NJ #2 48.67, the 4×800 team was second in 8:13.96, Uchenna Duru was third in the shot put with a a PR of 50-11 1/4, David Saggio placed fourth in the discus with a PR of 139-0, and Elijah Abraham placed fourth in the 400 hurdles in 58.21. Ryan McLaughlin was 6th in the 110 hurdles in a NJ #6 14.92.

In the 4×800, UC’s splits were 2:04.8 for Kyle Bartley, 2:01.0 for Justin Cadas, 2:02.5 for Andre Rodriguez, and 2:04.5 for Trevor Garrity.

UC girls dominate the Metuchen Relays with 9 wins, and 2 national qualifiers

Lufrano smashed meet record in 5K, Kwasnik had huge PR, and Morant and Evans shined

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls solidified its status as arguably the best track and field squad in New Jersey with a remarkable all-round performance at Saturday’s ninth annual Metuchen Relays.

It all started with Jerika Lufrano‘s sizzling meet and school record run in the 5K when she blasted a 17:45.79 to qualify for the New Balance Nationals, and ended with the Vikings winning the meet-concluding 4×400-meter relay in 4:07.98, the No. 4 time in N.J. this season.

In between those two first-place finishes, the Vikings won seven other events for a total of nine victories, qualified for New Balance Nationals in the 800 sprint medley, and racked up numerous NJ No. 1 performances.

On the track, sophomore Leena Morant and Khamil Evans were sensational for UC.

Morant split 2:16.0 to anchor the 4×800 to a come from behind victory in a NJ #2 9:42.47, and dropped a 58.5 on the winning 1,600 sprint medley that rna a NJ #2 4:15.64. Evans ran 24.9 on the winning 4×200 that ran a NJ #1 1:44.60, and split 58.1 as the anchor on the 800 sprint medley that place second in a NJ #2 1:49.71, which qualified for NB Nationals. UC also placed second in the 4×100 in a NJ #2 50.87

UC also dominated the hurdles as Brianna Ewing exploded with a big personal best and NJ #1 14.87 to win the 100 hurdles and placed second in the 400 hurdles, and Zamira Ysaac won the 400 hurdles in a NJ #1 1:06.00. Ysaac also anchored the winning SMR with a 2:23.8 carry.

In the field, Alexandra Kwasnik and Asiah Cooper scored big victories.

Kwasnik, a sophomore, continued her very impressive early season by clearing a personal best 5-2 to win the high jump and she just missed making 5-4. Cooper soared 34-3 to finish first in the triple jump.

UC places second in mixed 4×400 relay to earn All-American at New Balance Nationals

By Jim Lambert

NEW YORK – Union Catholic capped off a great weekend at the New Balance National Championships when the Vikings placed second in the first ever mixed 4×400-meter relay on Sunday to earn All-American honors at the New Balance Track and Field Center.

The Vikings foursome of Makay Johnson (50.9), Khamil Evans (56.5), Leena Morant (56.5), and Elijah Brown (48.7)) combined to run 3:33.22 to edge Bullis of Maryland, third in 3:33.24. Team War of Virginia won the race in 3:32.40.

The runner-up finish by Union Catholic gave the Vikings three All-American teams at the national meet. The boys 4×400 (fifth place) and the girls shuttle hurdles (sixth place) also earned All-American honors. A total of 12 UC athletes earned All-American status.

UC girls shuttle hurdle team earns All-American honors at New Balance Nationals

The squad of Ewing, Quainoo, Jordan and Williams combined to place 6th in 33.63

By Jim Lambert

NEW YORK – The Union Catholic girls made its presence felt once again at the New Balance Nationals when the shuttle hurdle team earned All-American status with a sixth place finish and the 4×800-meter relay squad placed seventh on Saturday at the New Balance Track and Field Center in the 168th Street Armory.

The foursome of Brianna Ewing, Felicia Quainoo, Avery Jordan and Angelique Williams teamed up to earn a spot on the podium in the shuttles with its sixth place finish in 33.63.

The Vikings narrowly missed another All-American finish in the 4×800 when Morgan Williams (2:20.8), Leena Morant (2:14.8), Zamira Ysaac (2:17.9.) andJerika Lufrano (2:20.9) placed seventh in the in 9:14.11, one place off the podium. UC also finished 22nd in the sprint medley relay in 4:15.00, and ran 1:43.10 in the trials of the 4×200.

content:
Union Catholic’s 4×400 wins record 4th straight title at Meet of Champions

Bennet-Jones, Evans, Ysaac and Morant combine on the victory

Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls, one of the most dominant track and field programs in recent state history, added to its remarkable legacy with a historic victory in the 4×400-meter relay at Saturday’s NJSIAA Meet of Champions at the Bennett Center in Toms River.

When UC sophomore Leena Morant crossed the finish line to put the finishing touches on the victory in 3:56.90, it gave the Vikings an unprecedented fourth straight M of C title in the 4×400. No boys or girls teams indoors or outdoors had ever won four straight 4×400 titles at the M of C. The Columbia girls captured three in a row twice indoors (1995-97 and 2012-14) and the UC boys won three in a row two indoors and outdoors from 2013-15.

Senior Mia Bennett-Jones led off the 4×400 with a split of 61.1. Junior Khamil Evans then ran 58.6 before handing off to sophomore Zamira Ysaac (59.4). Morant closed it out with a 58.4 carry.

UC had several other medal winners at the meet.

The 4×800 team of Alexandra Borik, Ashleigh Patterson, Ysaac, and Morgan Jackson placed third in the 4×800 in 9:28.97. Evans was eighth in the 400 in 58.21, and Morant placed fifth in the 800 in 2:15.45.

content:
UC girls T&F team stays perfect by winning fourth straight Non-Public A State title

The Vikings finished the season undefeated in team competition

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls track and field team put an exclamation point on its undefeated season with a dominating performance at Sunday’s NJSIAA Non-Public A Track and Field Championships at the Bennett Center in Toms River.

The Vikings received contributions from 12 different athletes and ran away with its fourth straight state title, 90-46 over runner-up Pingry.

With the victory, UC finished the season undefeated in team competition. On its march to perfection, the Vikings swept the Union County Track and Field and Relay titles, swept the State Non-Public A Track and Field and Relay championships, and captured the NJCTC title.

UC scored in nine of the 10 events, with its lone victory coming in the 4×400 with a time of 3:59.01, which makes the Vikings the No. 2 seed at this Saturday’s Meet of Champions at the Bennett Center.

In the 4×400, Brianna Ewing split 1:00.7, Leena Morant went 57.9, Mia Bennett-Jones ran 1:01.8, and Khamil Evans anchored in 59.4

Morant and Evans also added second-place finishes for UC. Morant broke her own school sophomore record by placing 2nd in the 800 in 2:17.73 as UC went 2-3-4 in the 2-lap race. Evans was second in the 400 in 58.22.

Jerika Lufrano had a huge day for UC. She placed third in the 1,600 in 5:10.60 and then came back to finish second in the 3,200 in 11:13.74.

In other highlights, Felicia Quianoo was second in the 55 hurdles in 8.59 (8.57 in the trials), Ewing placed third in the hurdles in 8.61, Morgan Williams was third in the 800 in 2:19.87, Zamira Ysaac placed fourth in the 800 in 2:20.18, Angelique Williams was third in the high jump (5-2), Christina Samuels placed 2nd in the shot put (34-0 1/2), Sophia Martinez was third in the shot put (33-9 3/4), and Sydney Tucker was third in the 55 dash in 7.47 (7.46 in the trials)

The Vikings will be back in action at the Eastern States Championships tomorrow (Tuesday) night at the New Balance Track and Field Center in New York, and then will compete at the state Meet of Champions this Saturday at the Bennett Center.

UC girls runaway with 5th straight Union County Track and Field Title

Several Vikings star to lead the team to dominating performance

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls kept its undefeated season going strong with another remarkable performance at Saturday’s Union County Track and Field Championships at the Jersey City Armory.

The Vikings, widely considered the No. 1 team in the state and one of the best in the nation, scored in all nine events and received points from 13 different athletes as they racked up 80 1/2 points to take home the team trophy. Union, Westfield and Gov. Livingston tied for second with 37 points.

Full results here and videos from the meet are here

There were lots of highlights for UC in this one. 

Sophomore Leena Morant placed second in both the 400 and 800 with sizzling times. Her 800 time of 2:18.71 is NJ #4 and her 400 time of 58.77 is a personal best and NJ #9. 

Junior Jerika Lufrano won the 3,200 in an unpushed and NJ #5 11:08.84.

Felicia Quainoo (8.58) and Brianna Ewing (8.60) went 2-3 in the 55 hurdles. Alexandra Borik placed fourth in the 1,600 in 5:32.08. Angelique Williams was second in the high jump (5-2) and Tyler Scott tied for fifth in the HJ at 4-10. Sydney Tucker placed sixth in the 55 dash in 7.48, Christina Samuels was third in shot put with a 33-9 3/4. Freshman Morgan Williams was third in the 800 in 2:19.75 and ran on the winning 4×400 (4:05.29). Zamira Ysaac finished fifth in the 800 in 2:22.23 and was on the first-place 4×400, and Khamil Evans was fourth in the 400 and ran on the relay. Ashleigh Patterson also contributed for UC by running  leg on the 4×4.

content:
UC girls sweep track events, steamroll to 4th straight Non-Public A Relay title

The Vikings defeated runner-up Paramus Catholic, 72-37

By Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls did it again!

In a performance that solidified its status as the top team in New Jersey, the Vikings threw down a remarkable display by sweeping all six track events and steamrolling its way to a 72-37 victory over runner-up Paramus Catholic to capture its fourth straight State Non-Public A Relay title on Thursday night at the Bennett Center in Toms River.

UC won the shuttle hurdles in a NJ #2 32.34, the distance medley in a school record and NJ #1 12:24.00, the sprint medley in 4:20.58, the 4×200 in 1:46.21, the 4×400 in 4:09.59, and the 4×800 in 9:41.47. In the field, the Vikings placed second in shot put and fourth in the high jump.

Several athletes had outstanding performances to lead the Vikings to the dominating victory.

Jerika Lufrano anchored the DMR with a 5:10.3 carry and ran 2:28.7 in the 4×800. Zamira Ysaac led off the DMR with a 3:52.6 split and ran 60.7 in the 4×400. Mia Bennet-Jones ran 61.4 in the DMR and 63.4 in the 4×400. Leena Morant went 2:19 in the DMR and 2:27 on the anchor of the SMR. Khamil Evans ran 25.6 in the 4×200 and 58.8 in the SMR. Brianna Ewing ran 7.7 in the shuttle hurdles and 26.6 in the 4×200. Sydney Tucker ran 26.5 in the 4×200 and 27.1 in the SMR. Felicia Quainoo ran 8.2 in the shuttles and 27.2 in the 4×200. Ashleigh Patterson split 63.1 in the 4×400 and 2:24 in the 4×800. Morgan Williams ran 62.1 in the 4×400 and split 2:24.5 in the 4×800. Angelique Williams ran 8.5 in the shuttles and cleared 5-0 in the high jump. In the shot put, Sophia Martinez threw a 33-1 1/2 and Christina Samuels had a 31-9.

“The goal was to sweep the track events like we did at the county meet,” said UC head girls track and field coach Mike McCabe. “We wanted to dominate on the track and go as big as we could in the fields, and just perform at our best. I’m really happy with the way so many girls stepped up for us.”

content:
UC girls nearly record a perfect score, roll to 5th straight Union County Relay title

The Vikings scored a meet record 76 out of a possible 80 points

Jim Lambert

The Union Catholic girls track and field team produced the most dominant performance in meet history when the Vikings nearly recorded a perfect score and smashed a meet record en route to winning the Union County Relay title for the fifth straight year on Sunday at the Jersey City Armory.

Full results of the meet

The Vikings won seven of the eight events, including NJ #1 times in the shuttle hurdles and sprint medley relay, and racked up a remarkable meet record 76 points out of possible 80 on the way to a 76-29 victory over runner-up Rahway. UC broke the meet record of 72 points that they set last year.

UC won the shuttle hurdles in a NJ #1 32.12, the sprint medley in a NJ #1 4:10.66, the distance medley in 12:34.79, the 4×200 in 1:46.19, the 4×400 in a meet record 4:05.67, the 4×800 in 10:04.23, and the high jump at 10-0. The only event UC didn’t win was the shot put where the Vikings placed third, led by Sophia Martinez‘s 35-1 1/4, which was the second best throw of the meet.

Sophomore Leena Morant had a huge day for UC with a 2:15.0 800 anchor split in the SMR, and a 59.2 carry in the 4×400. Jerika Lufrano ripped a 5:05 to anchor the winning DMR team, and Angelique Williams cleared a meet best 5-2 in the high jump.

The Vikings, who now own the top times in N.J. this season in the shuttle hurdles, 4×400, 4×800, SMR amd DMR, will be heavily favored to repeat as champions at this Thursday’s Non-Public State Relay Championships at 4 p.m. the Bennett Center in Toms River.

content:
UC TRACK AND FIELD STAR BRIANNA EWING SIGNS HER NATIONAL LETTER OF INTENT WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF MAINE

Scotch Plains, N.J. – Ewing is one of the top hurdlers in New Jersey
By Jim Lambert

Union Catholic’s Brianna Ewing, one of the state’s top hurdlers, signed her National Letter of Intent with the University of Maine on Wednesday morning during a ceremony in the main lobby of the school.

“This is very emotional for me,’’ said Ewing, who lives in Franklin. “I’ve been through a lot and worked very hard to reach this point. “The atmosphere here at Union Catholic really helped me achieve all my goals. To get a full ride is more than I ever imagined. I have my family, friends and teammates here to share this with. I’m just so jubilant right now.’’ 

Ewing has built a remarkable resume during her track and field career at Union Catholic, highlighted by several outstanding performances on the county, state and national level.

As a junior last spring, the versatile Ewing placed second in the 100-meter hurdles and third in the 400 hurdles at the Union County Championships, finished fourth in the high hurdles at the South Jersey, Non-Public A Championships, and placed fourth at the state Non-Public A Championships to qualify for the Meet of Champions.

Ewing has also excelled on the national stage as she ran a leg on Union Catholic’s shuttle hurdle team that placed second and ran on the sprint medley relay that placed fifth at the New Balance National Championships last June in North Carolina to earn All-American honors in both events.
For her career, Ewing has personal best times of 7.71 in the 55-meter dash, 8.50 in the 55 hurdles, 15.03 in the 100 hurdles, 26.01 in the 200, and 65.70 in the 400 hurdles, and she has also helped lead the Vikings to numerous county, conference and state titles.
Published November 15, 2017

author: Michael McCabe

excerpt: THE UNION CATHOLIC GIRLS CROSS-COUNTRY TEAM WON THE STATE TITLE IN DRAMATIC FASHION Holmdel, N.J. – The Vikings edged Red Bank Catholic, 63-65, to […]
content:
THE UNION CATHOLIC GIRLS CROSS-COUNTRY TEAM WON THE STATE TITLE IN DRAMATIC FASHION

Holmdel, N.J. – The Vikings edged Red Bank Catholic, 63-65, to win the state Non-Public A title on Saturday at Holmdel Park
By Jim Lambert
Trailing with a half mile to go with a state title hanging in the balance, the Union Catholic girls cross-country team dug down deep and staged a dramatic rally to edge Red Bank Catholic in thrilling fashion to capture its second NJSIAA Non-Public A title in three years on Saturday at Holmdel Park.
Junior Jerika Lufrano led the charge for the Vikings by placing second in a school record 18:51. Sophomore Leena Morant (9th in 20:15), junior Megan McCabe (15th in 20:32), sophomore Zamira Ysaac (16th in 20:32), and sophomore Zoe Lee (21st in 20:46) were the other scorers for UC, who all ran very gutsy over the final 800 meters to help the Vikings come from behind for a heart-pounding 63-65 victory over defending champion Red Bank Catholic. Sophomore Ashleigh Patterson and junior Monika Wlodarski were the No. 6 and No. 7 runners for UC.
A couple huge keys to the victory were that Morant finished two places and one second in front of an RBC runner, and Lee was one place and one second in front of another RBC runner. Lee, who fractured her tibia at the Group Championships at Holmdel last year, picked off three runners, including two from RBC, in the last 800 to help seal the race for the Vikings
The entire top five for UC, who averaged 20:11 (No. 2 in school history), ran significantly faster than they did at the Shore Coaches meet at Holmdel last month when the Vikings averaged 20:50.
“The girls raced as a complete team today,’’ said UC coach Mike McCabe, whose 2015 team won the first girls state title in UC history. “I’m extremely proud of how they raced for one another. It was a great win over a very strong team. We ran some runners down and held some off. It’s the best we have closed. Finishing is all about heart and they showed so much grit.’’
The victory was especially sweet for Megan McCabe, who has regained her form after battling through some iron issues and was a huge difference maker for the Vikings on their road to the state title.
“I just stayed positive and kept working hard through it all and things worked out,’’ said McCabe. It’s so satisfying to be able to help my team reach this goal. It really feels great to put in all the work and see it all pay off like this.’’
With its victory, the UC girls advanced to the state Meet of Champions next Saturday at Holmdel Park where they will aim to break the school record average of 20:05 that the 2015 team ran at the Meet of Champions when the Vikings placed fifth.
Published November 12, 2017

content:
UNION CATHOLIC TRACK AND FIELD STAR AMAYA CHADWICK SIGNS WITH PURDUE UNIVERSITY

Scotch Plains, N.J. – Chadwick is one of the state’s best hurdlers and sprinters
By Jim Lambert
Amaya Chadwick of Union Catholic, one of the biggest track and field stars in New Jersey, signed a National Letter of Intent with Purdue University on Wednesday morning during a ceremony in the main lobby in the school.
“This moment really means a lot to me,’’ said Chadwick, who was surrounded by family and friends and teammates during the ceremony. “I’m grateful that I was able to work hard and make myself, my coaches, my teammates and my family proud. I really loved the atmosphere at Purdue, and I felt the school fit me socially, athletically, and academically. The whole signing thing is very exciting and I’m happy to finally make it official.’’

During her remarkable track career at Union Catholic, Chadwick has established herself as one of the best hurdlers and sprinters in New Jersey.
Chadwick, who lives in Plainfield, has captured seven individual Union County championships and seven state titles indoors and outdoors combined in the hurdles and the sprints, including both the Non-Public A 100-meter dash and 100 hurdles titles each of the past two seasons. And she’s the school record holder in both the 55 dash and the 100 dash.
She has also placed second at the Meet of Champions three times in the high hurdles (twice outdoors and once indoors), ran the 200 leg on the national record national record breaking Swedish Relay last June to win her second national title, ran on Union Catholic’s 4×400 relay that was the top American finisher at the Penn Relays, and she has helped lead the Vikings to numerous indoor and outdoor state and county team championships.
Union Catholic track and field coach Mike McCabe said Purdue is getting a great one in Chadwick.
“Amaya is one of the most decorated hurdlers and sprinters in UC history, and she’s been a dash/hurdle double winner multiple times,’’ said Coach McCabe. “Her dominance is clear within our county and state. She’s the top returning hurdlers in the state and one of the top returners in the 100 dash. Amaya is one of the very best track and field athletes in New Jersey.’’
Published November 8, 2017

content:
Thursday, May 4th, 2017
Kehler Stadium, Westfield (Across the street from Edison Intermediate School)

Race Videos

Results: Boys | Girls

Westfield, N.J. – The UC girls won its third straight title while the boys captured its 6th in the past 7 years

By Jim Lambert
The Union Catholic track and field teams owned the Union County Relays on Saturday as the Vikings threw down several sizzling performances, highlighted by a state record by the girls in the 4×200, on the way to sweep of the team titles at Gary Kehler Stadium in Westfield.
The girls ran away with its third straight title, 125-58 over runner-up Westfield, and the boys outscored runner-up Elizabeth, 116-84, to win its 6th title in the past 7 years. Full results of the meet
In the girls 4×200, Sydney McLaughlin led off for UC with a 23.2 split. Khamil Evans followed with a 24.3. Then Amaya Chadwick went 24.7 and Sydney Tucker anchored in 25.2 to stop the clock at 1:37.53. That erased the 14-year-old state record of 1:37.77 set in 2003 by Franklin, and is No. 14 in the nation this season.

2017 ST County Relays – G4x200 from Michael McCabe on Vimeo.

The girls also won the 4×100 in a NJ #2 (47.72, the 4×400 (3:51.48), the shuttle hurdles in a NJ #1 59.46, the sprint medley in a NJ #1 4:03.67, the triple jump, the 400 hurdles, the high jump, and the long jump. The Vikings also placed second in the 4×800 (9:29.75), second in the 4×1,600 (22:28.25).
In the boys competition, lots of Vikings came up with personal best performances to ignite the attack.
Justin Cadas split 4:27 on the 4th place distance medley relay, 1:57.0 on the winning 4×800, and 4:27.5 on the first-place 4×1,600.
Ryan McLaughlin continued his breakout sophomore season with personal bests of 55.16 in the 400 hurdles and 20-4 in the long jump, and he also split 50.1 on the runner-up 4×400, and had a very strong leg on the winning shuttle hurdles (1:01.62).
Brandon Patterson came up huge in the field with personal best throws of 53-6 in the shot put and 134-7 in the discus, which was a 20 foot PR. Uchenna Duru also had a huge PR of 121-7 to help UC place 2nd in the discus.
Krishna White came up with a four foot PR of 46-1 in the triple jump and went 6-0 in the high jump. Isaac Eason cleared a PR of 6-0 in the high jump, and Conor Reilly had PR’s of 13-0 in the pole vault and 39-9 in the triple.

title: Sydney Runs on World Record DMR!
author: Michael McCabe
classList: post-12808 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-all-posts category-results category-winter-track-and-field
excerpt: Boston, Mass. – Union Catholic Olympian Sydney McLaughlin split 52.32 on the 400-meter leg on world record breaking distance medley relay at the New […]
content:
Boston, Mass. – Union Catholic Olympian Sydney McLaughlin split 52.32 on the 400-meter leg on world record breaking distance medley relay at the New Balance Grand Prix meet

By Jim Lambert

Union Catholic Olympian Sydney McLaughlin added to her remarkable track and field resume on Saturday when she ran on an all-star distance medley relay team that smashed the world record at the New Balance Indoor Grand Prix meet at the Reggie Lewis Center in Boston.

McLaughlin, an Olympian in the 400-meter hurdles this past summer, split 52.32on the 400-meter leg of the DMR as she combined with three other Olympians to finish first in 10:40.31, which shattered the world indoor record of 10:42.57 that was set in 2015.

The 17-year-old McLaughlin, the youngest U.S. track and field Olympian in 44 years, teamed up with Emma Coburn, Brenda Martinez, Jenny Simpson on the star-studded DMR in Boston.

Coburn, who won a bronze medal in the steeplechase at the Olympic Games this past summer, led off  the DMR with a 1,200 leg of 3:18.40. Then the Kentucky-bound McLaughlin, the national high school indoor 400 record holder, ran 52.32 for her two laps before handing off to Martinez in the lead. Martinez split 2:01.92 for 800, and then Simpson, the bronze medalist in the 1,500 in Rio, finished off the record breaking performance with a 4:27.66 anchor carry.

Congratulations, Sydney!!
From: http://www.unioncatholic.org/apps/news/article/664845

title: Vikings Sparkle at County Championship!
author: Michael McCabe
classList: post-12810 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-all-posts category-results category-winter-track-and-field
excerpt: Jersey City, N.J. – Junior Amaya Chadwick won 2 races at Saturday’s Union County Track and Field Championships at the Jersey City Armory The […]
content:
Jersey City, N.J. – Junior Amaya Chadwick won 2 races at Saturday’s Union County Track and Field Championships at the Jersey City Armory

The Union Catholic girls, led by double-winner Amaya Chadwick and Jerika Lufrano and Angelique Williams, ran away with its fourth straight title and the boys placed second at the Union County Championships on Saturday at the Jersey City Armory.

UC Olympian Sydney McLaughlin didn’t compete at the county meet because she’s in Boston running the 400 leg on an all-star distance medley relay that will attempt to break the world record on Saturday at 5:35 p.m.

Chadwick, a junior, won the 55-meter dash in 7.12 and the 55 hurdles in 8.00 to help lead the Vikings to an 87-34 victory over runner-up Cranford. Lufrano won the 1,600 (5:29.56) and was third in the 3,200 (12:18.79). Williams finished first in the high jump (5-4 and placed fourth in the hurdles.

Also for the UC girls, freshman Leena Morant also had a big day by placing second in the 800 (2:20.03) and third in the 400 (59.67).

In the boys competition, Union Catholic was led by Nate Papachristos, first in the 3,200 (9:47.30) and second in the 1,600 (4:31.90). The Vikings placed second to Elizabeth, 73 ½-56.

By Jim Lambert

Toms River, N.J. – The Vikings received several outstanding performances at Thursday’s NJSIAA Non-Public A Relays

The Union Catholic girls won the final two events on the track to secure its third straight title and the boys placed second at the NJSIAA Non-Public A Relay Championships on Thursday night at the Bennett Center in Toms River.

The UC girls were clinging to a 43-42 lead over Monmouth County powerhouse Red Bank Catholic when the Vikings closed out the meet by winning the sprint medley relay in 4:15.64 and the 4×400 relay in 4:03.75 to win the team title, 63-42, over runner-up RBC.

In addition to its victory in the SMR and 4×400, the UC girls also won the 4×200 in a N.J. No. 1 1:44.58, and the shuttle hurdles in 31.83, and placed second in the distance medley relay and third in the 4×800.

For the Vikings, Olympian Sydney McLaughlin ran 24.2 in the 4×200 and 55.8 for the 400 in the SMR. Amaya Chadwick led off the shuttle hurdles with a 7.6 and ran 26.2 in the 4×200. Felicia Quainoo ran 7.6 in the hurdles, 26.8 in the 4×200, and 61.8 in the 4×400. Leena Morant split 2:19.9 in the SMR, and  2:26.1 in the 4×800. Cassie Lamadieu ran 59.2 for 400 in the DMR, and 60.0 in the 4×400, and Jerika Lufrano anchored the DMR with a 5:20.2 carry and ran 2:29.4 in the 4×800.

On the boys side, the Vikings had a strong meet, placing second in the distance medley, 4×800 and 4×400 on the way to a runner-up finish to defending champion Christian Brothers Academy, 86-52. In the DMR, UC’s time of 10:29.49 is No. 3 in N.J. this season.

For UC, freshman Elijah Brown had a strong meet for UC, splitting 52.5 for his 400 leg in the distance medley, and ran 50.9 in the 4×400. Justin Cadas anchored the DMR with a 4:24.5 carry and ran 2:01.3 in the SMR. Freshman Conor Reilly cleared 12-0 in the pole vault. Greg Gibbs ran 1:58.5 for 800 in the SMR. Nate Papachristos ran 3:12.8 in the DMR and 2:02.1 in the 4×800, and Makay Johnson split 22.5 in the 4×200, and 50.9 in the 4×400.

By Jim Lambert

By Jim Lambert
Olympian Sydney McLaughlin added to her remarkable track and field resume on Saturday when the Union Catholic senior torched the track by breaking her own New Jersey record and running the No. 2 high school time ever in the girls 300-meter run at the Molloy Stanner Games at the New Balance Track and Field Center in New York.

The Kentucky-bound McLaughlin, who became the youngest U.S. track and field Olympian in 44 years this past summer, stopped the clock at 37.11 to smash her state record of 37.49 that she ran as a sophomore in 2015. Congratulations, Sydney!

Wednesday, November 9th, 2016

End of Season Time Trial

All members of the Cross Country Team are expected be at practice on Wednesday (11/9). There will be a 1600m Time Trial for all athletes who are not competing at the state meet. This is a great way to see how far you have come since the early season Time Trial!

THOSE WHO ARE NOT TRAINING FOR THE STATE MEET, DO NOT HAVE PRACTICE ON MONDAY OR TUESDAY. But an easy run on Tuesday is highly recommended. Will help you run fast on Wednesday.

If you are running the Time Trial, please bring your uniform to return  on Wednesday.

Also, bring your racing spikes. We will run the Time Trial on the track.

You ARE running the Time Trial, unless you are on the following list.

If you are on this list, you will be training for the State Meet and  not running the Time Trial :

title: Amari Onque-Shabazz to Villanova
author: Michael McCabe
classList: post-13596 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-all-posts category-awards category-spring-track-and-field category-winter-track-and-field
excerpt: Amari Onque-Shabazz of Union Catholic has made her college choice. The winner is….Villanova Amari Onque-Shabazz of Union Catholic, one of the state’s biggest track […]
content:
Amari Onque-Shabazz of Union Catholic has made her college choice. The winner is….Villanova

Amari Onque-Shabazz of Union Catholic, one of the state’s biggest track and field stars, announced that she will attend Villanova next year. (Steve Hockstein | For NJ Advance Media)
By Jim Lambert | NJ Advance Media for NJ.com
on October 21, 2015 4:24 PM, updated October 21, 2015 7:30 PM

Amari Onque-Shabazz of Union Catholic, one of the state’s biggest track and field stars, has made a verbal college commitment, her coach Mike McCabe said on Wednesday.

The winner is………….Villanova!!!!

Onque-Shabazz also had offers from Michigan, Richmond, and Northeastern.

Onque-Shabazz, who has remarkable range, has put together a remarkable resume during her high school days, highlighted by an outdoor season last spring that was simply remarkable.

As a junior this past spring, Onque Shabazz won the 800 at the Meet of Champions by running a personal best 2:10.03, ran a 400 PR of 56.14, split 54.2 on the Union Catholic 4×400 that won the New Balance National title in 3:35.90, a NJ state record and No. 2 in U.S. history, earned All-American honors in the SMR, and ran a PR of 5:05.27 in the 1,600.

That’s not all.

Onque-Shabazz is also a very strong cross-country runner. On Tuesday she ran 19:29 to win the Mountain Division title at the Union County Conference Championships to help UC capture the team title, and she has a Holmdel Park PR of 19:08. Led by Onque-Shabazz, the Union Catholic XC team is currently ranked No. 8 in the state.

CONGRATS, AMARI!!!

GET UR WILDCATS ON!!!!

content:
New Balance Indoor National Championship
Friday, March 14th – Sunday, March 16th, 2014

The Union Catholic Boys and Girls teams put on a show at the 2014 Indoor National Meet! The boys repeated as 4×200 and 4×400 National Champions, while the girls earned the first relay All-American honors for UC by placing 4th int the 4×200!

Photo Gallery  |  NBIN Youtube Video Channel |  NJ.com Article |  NJRunners Article  | Courier News Article

Highlights
-1st Place – Boys 4×200 Relay – 3:15.53 – State Record, US#8 All-Time
-1st Place – Boys 4×400 Relay – 1:27.04 – NJ#2 All-Time, US#4 All-Time
-2nd Place – Boys Shuttle Hurdle Relay – 29.52 – NJ#2 All-Time, US#4 All-Time
-3rd Place – Boys Sprint Medley Relay – 3:26.16 – Union County Record, NJ#2  All-Time, US#8 All-Time
-4th Place – Girls 4×200 Meter Relay – 1:40.51 – Union County Record, NJ#4 All-Time

content:
Friday, March 14th – Sunday, March 16th, 2014
Armory Track & Field Center, NY

Notes
-Plan your meals, snacks and drinks for each day.
-Get proper rest. Hydrate!
-We will be car pooling to the meet throughout the weekend. Stay in contact with Coach McCabe about your transportation.
-BE ON TIME!!! If you have an issue, contact call Coach McCabe on his cell.
-Our schedule, entries and arrival times are listed below.
-When you arrive at the track for the first time, call Coach McCabe so he can bring your bib number down. Your bib is what will allow entry into the meet. Bring it back each day or you won’t be admitted.
-Don’t forget your racing spikes and remember to put in 1/4 inch pyramid spikes (Coach has extra).
-Bring the proper uniform. If you are unsure. Bring more than one uniform.
-Make sure Coach McCabe has your USATF #

—————————————————————————————————————————————————

 

Volunteers – Please arrive to UC between 10:30am – 11:00am on Sunday morning. Thank You

Coaches

Thank you for choosing to attend the Union Catholic Track & Field Invitational! Our meet is this SUNDAY, APRIL 21st beginning at 1:00pm (Teams may report as early as 11:30am). We hope you enjoy your time at UC! We will run the meet as fast as possible! There will be concessions available (bagels, pretzels, drinks, etc.) As of today, the weather looks solid for Sunday. If for any reason we need to cancel, I will send an email and post onwww.uctrack.com no later than 10:00am on Sunday morning.  Final Instructions are below.

If you have any last minute questions, I can be reached at mmccabe@unioncatholic.org or 908-370-7666

Mike McCabe


FINAL INSTRUCTIONS

Parking Options
The Parking Lot on the Left Side of Union Catholic
The Driveway in Front of Union Catholic
At 1:15pm – Parking will be available at Immaculate Heart of Mary Church across the street from UC.

Team Seating/Tents
All teams are asked to setup their tents in the parking lot on the gym side.
No tents or team setup will be permitted on the back driveway
The driveway needs to be clear for emergencies

Labels
Pre-Printed Labels will be provided to each team at the meet, once payment is received. There will be 3 pre-printed labels for each athlete on your team’s roster. Coaches will need to write the event on each label.

Coaches’ Meeting
There will be a brief Coaches’ Meeting at 12:45pm on the infield, next to the finish line tent. We ask that at least one coach from each team be at the meeting.

Heat Sizes

100m Fun Run – 15-20 per heat
200m – 1 Athlete per lane, 6 lanes. (Will Start at the 100m Start)
400m – No Lanes – 10-12 athletes per heat
800m – No Lanes – 12-15 athletes per heat
1600m – No Lanes – 12-15 athletes per heat
Sprint Medley Relay (4-1-1-2) – No Lanes – 8-12 teams per heat

Seeding Heats
Coaches please make your athletes aware of who you want to run in the faster heats. Also, you are welcome to come to the staging area to make the Clerk aware of which of your athletes you want seeded first.

Awards
-Medals will be placed into a bag for each team. At the end of the meet these bags will be distributed to a team representative.
-1st place and Runner-Up Trophies will be awarded at the end of the meet.

Additional Rules
-You may run 1st or 2nd graders in a higher division, if you feel they will be competitive
-Athletes can run in higher divisions, but cannot run in a lower division
-Girls can race in Boys relays, but boys cannot race in girls relays.
-Athletes are allowed any 3 events (The relay counts as one of these events)
-Relay Batons will be provided

 

FIELD EVENTS
Rules
Shot Put will be setup in Flights – 3 Throws , No Finals
Long Jump will be setup in Flights – 2 Jumps, No Finals
Javelin will not have Flights. Athletes will get 3 consecutive throws.

Open Pit Times
